chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Ma'la ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:

A letter came from Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) when al-Zubayri was killed: 'This is the recompense for one who fabricated lies against Allah and His close friends. He presumed that he would kill me while I have no offspring. So how did he witness the might of Allah?' A son was born to him and he named him Muhammad, in the year two hundred and fifty-six.

key_terms.الزُّبَيْرِيُّ: Al-Zubayri, a specific individual whose death is narrated

ai.seo_question: What was the significance of al-Zubayri's death in relation to the Imam's offspring?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the divine vindication of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) against the specific claim of al-Zubayri that he would die childless, framing the latter's death as recompense for fabricating lies against Allah and His representatives. The birth of his son, Muhammad, in 256 AH not only confirmed the continuation of the Imamate but also established the lineage of the Awaited Imam, a key proof in Shia eschatology. This event underscores the theme of divine power overriding human skepticism regarding the preservation of the Prophet's progeny.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 198 - Narrated Muhammad bin Yaqub from Husain bin Muhammad Ashari from Mualla Ibn Muhammad from Ahmad bin Muhammad that:

When Zubairi was killed, a letter came from Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) as follows: “This is the punishment of one who attributes lies to Allah, the Exalted, with respect to His close friends. He presumed that he would kill me while I do not have an offspring. So how did he witness the might of Allah?” He sired a son and named him Muhammad. This was in the year two hundred and fifty-six.
